sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento del VIX (+2.64%) e della debolezza dei mercati azionari, con S&P 500 in calo dello 0.02% e STOXX 600 in calo dello 0.62%. Il DXY è stabile (+0.13%) e il prezzo del petrolio è in rialzo (+0.03%). La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi invariati, ma ha segnalato rischi fiscali e geopolitici.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the increase in VIX (+2.64%) and weakness in equity markets, with S&P 500 down 0.02% and STOXX 600 down 0.62%. DXY is stable (+0.13%) and oil prices are rising (+0.03%). The ECB has kept rates unchanged but flagged fiscal and geopolitical risks.

market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are weak, with S&P 500 down 0.02% and STOXX 600 down 0.62%. VIX is rising (+2.64%) and DXY is stable (+0.13%). Oil prices are up (+0.03%) and TLT is down (-0.24%).

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dello 0.5%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.1%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.02%, il VIX è salito del 2.6%. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.1%, a 99.34 L'oro è sceso dello 0.7%, a 4418 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio è salito dello 0.03%, a 94.32 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale USA è in calo dello 0.3%, al 4.48%. Il BTP 10Y italiano è stabile, al 3.73%.

La situazione in Iran e le tensioni in Ucraina continuano a influenzare i mercati. La Corea del Sud ha dichiarato che l'boom dell'AI potrebbe mitigare gli impatti negativi delle tensioni geopolitiche. L'ECB ha avvertito che i rischi fiscali e geopolitici potrebbero essere sottovalutati dai mercati.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin scende del 3,22% a settantatremila dollari. I flussi degli ETF mostrano una outflow di centoquarantacinque milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche di mercato e dalle notizie geopolitiche. 

  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende del 4,40% a duemila dollari, Solana perde il 3,33% a ottantadue dollari e BNB scende del 2,88% a seicentotrentaquattro dollari.

  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 22, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed down 0.5%, Shanghai up 0.1%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 closed up 0.02%, the VIX rose 2.6%. The Dollar Index is up 0.1%, at 99.34 Gold fell 0.7%, to $4,418 per ounce. Oil rose 0.03%, to $94.32 The 10-year US yield is down 0.3%, to 4.48%. The Italian 10Y BTP is stable, at 3.73%. The situation in Iran and tensions in Ukraine continue to influence markets. South Korea stated that the AI boom could mitigate the negative impacts of geopolitical tensions. The ECB warned that fiscal and geopolitical risks might be underestimated by markets. No major macro data out today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin falls 3.22% to $73,000 ETF flows show an outflow of $145 million. This movement could be influenced by recent market dynamics and geopolitical news. Among altcoins, Ethereum falls 4.4% to $2,000, Solana loses 3.33% to $82, and BNB falls 2.88% to $634 The Fear & Greed Index is at 22, in Extreme Fear zone, suggests caution for investors. No macro data on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thanks for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

This event explores the path toward a new European social contract, one centered on renewed economic strategy, resilience, solidarity,…

articles.title: Control Without Ownership: How China’s Party-Business Networks Dominate Indonesia’s Mineral Supply Chains
articles.snippet: In 2024, when Jiangsu Delong, the world’s second-largest stainless-steel producer, filed for bankruptcy, several Chinese firms and state-owned enterprises quietly absorbed its Indonesian assets. Among them was China First Heavy Industries, a state-owned enterprise founded in 1954 as one of China’s early Soviet-backed industrial projects. Today, China First Heavy Industries supplies military-grade metals to China’s military, including reactor vessels for nuclear submarines. articles.title: A Sea Control Revolution?
articles.snippet: Sea control has changed. In recent years, there has been a quiet revolution in maritime strategy that has seen navies increasingly expected to exert greater levels of control over more of the world’s oceans, more of the time. Whether it is NATO forces protecting critical maritime infrastructure in the Baltic, Pacific Island nations requiring maritime domain awareness to protect against illegal fishing, or Chinese coast guard and maritime militia vessels occupying features in the South China Sea, navies across the globe are confronting major challenges and are being forced to operate in new and novel ways. articles.title: What does it mean to be "European" today?
articles.snippet: The idea of Europe as a community emerged many centuries ago, but its meaning keeps changing—to Europeans and non-Europeans alike. Juliet Johnson has pioneered research on the changing role of European symbols such as the 12-starred flag, designed in the 1950s and formally adopted by European institutions in the 1980s. Intriguingly, shifts in meaning have often first occurred on Europe's eastern side, before being adopted by Europe's western "core." What does it mean to be European today, in a fast-changing geopolitical environment and amid debates on which new member countries the European…

articles.snippet: Global oil inventories are fast approaching a critical point, with Asia the first facing “minimum operational levels” and Europe close behind. It seems the world is running out of time to avert a much bigger crisis than we already have. Asia is already struggling with supply, Jeff Currie, Senior Advisor at the Carlyle Group, told CNBC this week. Speaking on the sidelines of an industry event…

articles.title: Middle East Crisis Accelerates U.S.-Thailand LNG Supply Talks
articles.snippet: The sudden halt of liquefied natural gas (LNG) flows from the Middle East has prompted Asian buyers to seek long-term solutions to secure supply from sources not needing the blocked Strait of Hormuz. As Qatar’s LNG shipments are under force majeure until at least mid-August and full LNG export capacity may not be restored for another five years, LNG customers are looking to sign long-term supply deals with exporters outside of conflict areas.
